input: The adsorption of a dye from water onto a metal-organic framework was investigated by means of batch tests carried out at 298 K, and the results obtained provide a useful picture of the performance of the material under the conditions studied. The measurements were made with the dye in water throughout, so the solvent is the same in every test reported here. When the data were fitted to the Langmuir model, the fitted capacity came out at 254 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 6, which represents the saturation capacity implied by the model for this particular system. In a further set of measurements, an adsorbent dose of 1.1 g L-1 was employed, and it was found that the removal achieved after 120 min corresponded to 93% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1, leaving a residual concentration of 3.5 mg L-1 in the treated water. It is important to bear in mind that the Langmuir fit is reported for pH 6 only, and that the capacity at other pH values was not measured, so the fitted figure should not be taken to apply beyond the conditions under which it was obtained.
target: Adsorption of a dye from water on a metal-organic framework was measured in batch tests at 298 K. The fitted Langmuir capacity was 254 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 6. The capacity is a fitted parameter of the Langmuir model at the stated pH: it is the saturation uptake the model assigns to the adsorbent under the test conditions, not a directly weighed loading. At an adsorbent dose of 1.1 g L-1, removal after 120 min was 93% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1, a residual concentration of 3.5 mg L-1. The removal figure is stated against the initial concentration at the stated dose and contact time. The two figures describe different things. The capacity is a property of the fitted isotherm at saturation; the removal is an outcome at one dose and one contact time, and it falls short of the capacity whenever the residual concentration keeps the surface short of saturation. A higher dose or a longer contact time would change the removal figure without changing the capacity, and the two figures must not be interchanged. The batch tests were made in water at the stated temperature, and the reported values belong to that medium and that temperature. The Langmuir fit is reported for pH 6 only; capacity at other pH values was not measured, and the capacity figure does not extend to them.
